scope: Best bounded East African irrigation-capacity case found, retained outside training because the maximum system postdates 1500

promotion_audit.decision: Engaruka is a high-quality physical validation case but not a training anchor. The irrigation system began in the early 1400s and was in use by 1500, yet its most extensive occupation was 1620-1720. The 8,000-10,000 support estimate refers to the completed ancient field system, so assigning it to 1337 would silently import later landscape development.

records.label: Engaruka irrigated landscape, northern Tanzania
records.interval_semantics: Westerberg et al. report an archaeological platform-based population of 7,000-12,000 and separately calculate that 1,000 ha could support about 8,000 people, with as many as 10,000 supported when the whole system was used while retaining a trade surplus (p. 307). These quantities are retained separately and are not treated as a 1337 observation.
pressure_evidence: Westerberg et al. (2010), pp. 306-307: the land-use system covered about 2,000 ha, may have been one continuous settlement, and platform counts imply 7,000-12,000 people.
Westerberg et al. (2010), p. 307: a transparent cereal-yield and consumption calculation supports about 8,000 people on 1,000 ha and up to 10,000 on the whole usable system with surplus for trade.
Westerberg et al. (2010), pp. 307-309: the irrigation system was in use by 1500 and probably several decades earlier; the authors date initiation to the early 1400s.
Westerberg et al. (2010), pp. 310-314: the system persisted through prolonged dry conditions and trade breakdown, with local soil and water management identified as crucial to maintaining production.
records.trade_dependence: mixed, but the cited agricultural calculation explicitly supports the resident population locally and allows a surplus for neighboring pastoralists and caravans
records.boundary_description: The approximately 2,000 ha ancient Engaruka field, canal and terraced settlement system between the Olemelepo and Engaruka river fans; not the entire Tanzanian Rift Valley.
records.boundary_source: Westerberg et al. (2010), Figure 3 and pp. 306-309
records.source_family_independence: archaeological survey, radiocarbon chronology and transparent agricultural support calculation in one integrated source family
records.notes: Strong holdout for whether the model can represent a small, high-output African irrigation system without a regional correction. It remains validation-only because the published maximum population and completed-system capacity are not demonstrated for 1100-1500, even though the technology began inside that window.
